0.long_answer: Gram-negative bacteria are characterized by having a thin layer of peptidoglycan and an outer membrane, which prevents them from retaining the crystal violet stain during Gram staining. In contrast, Gram-positive bacteria have a thicker peptidoglycan layer that retains the stain. Malakoplakia, a chronic inflammatory condition often associated with complicated urinary tract infections, is typically linked to Gram-negative bacterial infections, most notably those caused by Escherichia coli.
